items.title: Crimean Bridge damage reported as rail and road traffic suspended
items.summary: Russia's transport authorities reportedly suspended both train and vehicle traffic across the Crimean Bridge while specialists assessed damage following an alleged Ukrainian strike. Images circulating online appear to show a collapsed section, but the extent of structural damage remains unverified; preliminary information indicated no casualties.

items.title: Russian security service alleges disruption of planned coordinated attacks
items.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service says it thwarted a purported Ukrainian-backed plot for simultaneous attacks inside Russia, alleging the seizure of more than 700 kilograms of explosives, at least 40 drones and six jet skis. The allegations, including the claimed Ukrainian intelligence involvement and quantities seized, have not been independently verified.

items.title: Russia alleges overnight strikes hit Ukrainian drone and aircraft-engine plants
items.summary: Russian military statements allege that overnight strikes hit two Kyiv facilities involved in attack-drone production, Techno-Links and Ukrplastic, as well as the Motor Sich and Ivchenko-Progress aircraft-engine plants in Zaporizhzhia. The reported hits, facilities' military roles and extent of any damage have not been independently verified.

items.title: Ukraine says North Korea supplies Russia with dozens of ballistic missiles monthly
items.summary: Ukraine's president says North Korea is supplying Russia with dozens of ballistic missiles each month, allowing Pyongyang to refine its weapons through use in the war. He called for Ukraine to receive comparable capabilities to counter the threat. The stated delivery rate has not been independently verified.

items.title: Ukraine details multi-weapon operation against Crimean Bridge
items.summary: Ukraine's president has claimed responsibility for the latest strikes on the Crimean Bridge, describing weeks of preparatory attacks on air defences and electronic-warfare systems. He said Ukrainian forces used Neptune and FP-5 Flamingo missiles alongside Palyanytsia and Ruta weapons against road and railway sections. Reports of collapsed spans and an arch remain unverified, as does the full extent of damage.

items.title: Emergency electricity outages affect multiple Ukrainian regions
items.summary: Electricity disruptions were reported across several Ukrainian regions, including Odesa, Mykolaiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Rivne, Sumy, Chernihiv and Chernivtsi. Emergency shutdowns were reportedly introduced in Kirovohrad, Poltava and Sumy regions following significant equipment damage. The precise causes, scale and expected restoration times have not been independently confirmed.

items.title: Russia opens investigation and warns against travel to Crimean Bridge
items.summary: Russian authorities have reportedly opened a terrorism investigation into the November 16–17 attacks on the Crimean Bridge and urged motorists to avoid approaching the crossing. Officials say security will be increased along the overland route to Crimea and maintain that supplies remain intact, while the Kremlin has pledged to rebuild the damaged bridge. The full extent of structural damage and the reliability of alternative supply routes remain unverified.

items.title: Hungary reportedly suspends rail services to Ukraine for two days
items.summary: Rail traffic between Hungary and Ukraine is reportedly being suspended for November 17–18 after a drone landed about 300 metres from a station in Mukachevo. The incident reportedly prompted the evacuation of a Hungarian train crew; the drone's origin and whether anyone was injured remain unclear.

items.title: Kyiv sets up additional emergency heating centres amid energy disruptions
items.summary: Local authorities in Kyiv are reportedly installing emergency heating centres in the Troieshchyna district as the city continues to face energy disruptions. Portable sanitation facilities are also planned, although the number of operational centres and their capacity have not been confirmed.

items.title: Kyiv's Southern Bridge reportedly reopens partially after strikes
items.summary: Traffic on Kyiv's Southern Bridge has reportedly resumed in one direction, from the left bank to the right, with vehicle-weight and spacing restrictions. The opposite direction reportedly remains closed because of damage, while the Northern Bridge is also said to have sustained damage. The extent of both bridges' structural damage has not been independently confirmed.

items.title: French military training mission inside Ukraine draws political scrutiny
items.summary: A reported French mission known as Volia has allegedly placed small teams of military instructors inside Ukraine to train personnel and maintain French-supplied weapons, including Caesar artillery and Mirage aircraft. The account has prompted a French opposition politician to demand parliamentary scrutiny and an end to the deployment; the mission's scope and legal status remain disputed.

items.title: Finnish president urges direct European talks with Putin
items.summary: Finnish President Alexander Stubb reportedly called for European leaders to engage directly with Vladimir Putin rather than leave negotiations over the war to other powers. He warned that Europe risks being excluded from decisions affecting its security and argued that any eventual agreement would require Russia's participation.
